approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and chooses its prior checkpoint using a fixed holdout. Each objective starts from a fresh trainable copy while the reference prior stays frozen. The best half of the current scored batch trains alongside a uniform sample from a memory of the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, using their original strings and the existing prior-likelihood-plus-reward target. New molecules come directly from ancestral token sampling and pass chemical validation and canonical duplicate checks. Its tokenizer keeps chlorine and bromine together but writes every bracket atom character by character, separating an atom from its charge or attached-hydrogen notation.
approach.novelty: Make each bracket atom observed in the unlabeled corpus one indivisible language token. This gives the recurrent model a complete atom-state unit, such as aromatic nitrogen with hydrogen or charged oxygen, at one prediction step and one subsequent context step. Ordinary SMILES characters and the existing chlorine and bromine tokens remain available, including a reversible character fallback for a bracket form absent from the learned vocabulary. The lineage has previously added historical elite replay; it has not tested this atom-state representation. The experiment asks whether complete bracket units are learned and retained in later valid novel chemistry while all memory, reward updates and sampling rules stay the same.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-15499bde2e65 models a bracket atom such as [nH], [N+] or [O-] as several independently emitted characters, although the expression jointly specifies one atom and its hydrogen or charge state. Its source has only Cl and Br compound tokens. The actual per-task generation logs sum to 3,345 RDKit-invalid strings among 34,960 raw draws across three completed seeds, plus two unterminated strings. Invalid strings were not retained, so their bracket-specific cause remains a hypothesis. The Parent molecular assessment reports uneven control of nitrogen functional state and unusual chemical forms alongside recognizable scaffold families. A read-only audit of the supplied unlabeled corpus found 218,284 of 1,272,851 rows containing bracket atoms, with 65 distinct bracket expressions: [nH] occurs 157,990 times, [O-] 64,949 and [N+] 63,675. These counts precede inherited length exclusion. The corpus contains no @, slash or backslash stereo markers, so this proposal does not claim to learn absent stereochemical labels. The Parent three-seed macro mean is 0.5075540530185733 with SD 0.01151827890752029; successful exact-sequence historical replay is inherited.
hypothesis: Coalesce each corpus-observed complete bracket-atom expression into one reversible SMILES token, with inherited Cl/Br-and-character fallback for unseen bracket expressions, so prior learning and its shared sequence interface model an atom together with its explicit hydrogen and charge state.

finding_summary.headline: Bracket-atom context learning improves, but the three-seed search mean does not
finding_summary.insights: Learning coherent atom-state units is supported, but better likelihood on those units does not ensure that objective-driven generation retains or exploits more of them. Accepted original strings containing bracket atoms actually fall from 1,269 to 835 out of 4,350 proposals; charged forms also become less common. The output still reaches recognizable medicinal scaffold families, while the Molecular assessment finds excessive low-scoring growth, reactive outliers and unspecified configurations. The experiment therefore narrows the unresolved issue to how a learned representation interacts with the existing search dynamics and chemical coverage, rather than a failure to encode or learn the registered units. The reduction in aggregate invalid strings does not identify bracket syntax as the Parent error source because rejected strings were not saved. No stereochemical supervision exists in this corpus, and none is created by the representation. The panel varies both preparation and search by seed, so it cannot isolate which stage caused the mixed task effects.
finding_summary.results: The new representation was used and learned in all three seeds. Every one of the 1,272,851 eligible corpus strings round-trips exactly, and the original training/holdout membership is preserved. Each holdout contains 1,013 complete bracket targets; their average negative log likelihood falls from about 5.08–5.14 before training to 2.07–2.27 after training. On identical holdout molecules, the learned prior also assigns better normalized likelihood to bracket-bearing sequences than the Parent in every seed. Prior freezing, fresh objective state and all online replay/update methods remain intact. Across the search panel, the raw invalid-string fraction falls from 9.568% to 8.573%, and both implementations complete every required batch. That local improvement does not yield the expected score gain: the macro mean is 0.506571 versus 0.507554, a paired change of -0.000983 rather than the registered increase of at least 0.002. Seed changes are -0.022179, +0.002069 and +0.017160. Gains in three task means are offset mainly by a 0.058039 decline in the sitagliptin mean, present in all three seeds. The smaller observed score SD, 0.004690 versus 0.011518, is descriptive evidence from this panel, not a reliability guarantee.

molecular.headline: Recognizable medicinal families dominate the leaders, with unresolved stereochemistry and extreme low-scoring growth
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Against Parent n-15499bde2e65, the output retains broad conventional aromatic, amide, sulfonamide and amine chemistry, while changing which families dominate individual seeds. High-scoring compounds mostly have familiar neutral C/N/O/S bonding and plausible medicinal scaffolds. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9759 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token presence from 0.9494 to 0.9908. Charge-token presence is low but nonzero; such tokens include nitro and other formal-charge representations and do not demonstrate appropriate protonation of basic amines. Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout. Structural diversity is broad, including fused heteroaromatics, cyclic and acyclic amines, sulfonamides, carbonyl-rich rings and occasional carbohydrate, lipid or peptide-like products. Apparent synthesis is plausible for many leading structures, with important exceptions among reactive and elaborate outliers. The low-scoring tail includes tiny fragments, very long alkyl chains, oversized multiaryl or peptide-like assemblies and isolated unusual valence patterns. These are not uniformly useful drug-like molecules, even when familiar groups recur. The report describes this output and its score associations without assigning mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring region contains moderately sized aromatic carbonyl compounds: a fused aza-aromatic nitrile bearing isopropoxy and fluoroanilide groups, indole carboxamides, diaryl ureas, and a naphthyl/azine carboxamide attached to morpholine. Another strong family contains arylidene nitrile and amide or enamide connectivity. These are mostly recognizable synthetic targets; the activated unsaturated nitrile compounds have potential electrophilicity and unspecified alkene geometry. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9897 and mean SMILES length is 38.8. The Parent also favored indole/carboxamide chemistry, including an N-methyl benzylamide; the current seeds broaden those carbonyl arrangements rather than revealing a wholly new chemical class.
liabilities: Activated unsaturated nitrile/carbonyl groups may be electrophilic, and their alkene geometry is unspecified.
Large multiaryl assemblies, highly lipophilic chains and occasional phosphonium or cationic aza-aromatic variants extend beyond the properties of the favorable neutral series.
missing_features: The high-scoring carbonyl/nitrile region lacks systematic stable alternatives to the activated arylidene nitrile linkage, with explicit alkene geometry where applicable.
Compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements are not consistently retained in the broader proposal stream; no unique missing target pharmacophore follows from the displayed examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best fused aza-aromatic nitrile/anilide scores 0.475614712250357. The Parent maximum was 0.5280588545286916 in a related indole carboxamide family, although the current maxima improve over the other paired Parent seeds. A cyanoacrylamide and a changed enamide connection tie at 0.4697065314067379. Very large aromatic assemblies and long aliphatic chains score poorly, as does the small thioaldehyde-amide at 5.6865747950850954e-18. A final chlorinated cyanoacrylamide scores only 0.01086772025284379 despite sharing the broad functional-group class. The visible gradient supports bounded size and specific aromatic/carbonyl/nitrile arrangement, not simply adding nitriles or rings.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 concentrates on a large fused nitrogen heteroaromatic lactam with aryl substituents, alkoxy or methylthio groups and ester, ketone or amide side chains. Fluorinated phenyl rings are common. Other seeds reach aza-heteroaryl/aniline and nitrile-rich families, including pyrrolidine-substituted heterocycles. Aromatic and ring-closure token presence are both 0.9908, and halogen presence is 0.6575. These generally have conventional bonding and plausible synthetic building blocks, but some are densely aromatic and heavily substituted. Compared with the Parent hydrazone/anilino, polyaryl and sulfur-containing families, the current strongest seed uses a more consistent fused aza-lactam core.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic surface, fluorinated phenyl groups and long acyl substituents can increase lipophilicity and reduce solubility.
Some other-seed hydrazone or highly substituted multiaryl products introduce isomerism and reactive functionality despite generally conventional chemistry.
missing_features: Broader compact scaffold alternatives retaining the favored nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic attachment pattern are underrepresented among the highest-scoring molecules.
The late family does not establish which peripheral aromatic, alkyl or halogen groups can be simplified without losing the useful core arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best acyl-substituted fused heterocycle scores 0.6258169934640523 versus the paired Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.5913471190523991. The shift is not uniform across seeds. Ester/alkoxy/methylthio variants tie at 0.6134179161860822, and different alkyl ketone lengths tie at 0.6118800461361015. Highly fluorinated aryl sulfone chemistry can be low, including 0.28938327467739233, while tiny fragments remain near 0.5004. Thus halogenation or molecule size alone does not explain the favorable region; the fused nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement and its attached aromatic groups appear more consequential than several peripheral substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders are recognizable aromatic basic-amine compounds. Seed 1 combines a branched aryl ketone chain with an N-substituted piperidinol bearing chlorophenyl groups; other leaders use arylamino piperidines, piperazines and aminoalkyl chains. Seed 2 grows long N-alkyl substituents on aryl aminoalcohols. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9655 and halogen presence is 0.7621. The Parent likewise produced high-scoring aryl cyclic amines, so the broad chemical preference persists with changed ring/linker arrangements. Most leaders have plausible synthesis and ordinary valence, but flexibility, lipophilic bulk and stereochemical ambiguity remain substantial.
liabilities: Multiple chlorinated aromatic groups, long N-alkyl chains and high flexibility create physicochemical and metabolic liabilities.
Unspecified stereochemistry and occasional triazene or other reactive outliers limit confidence in a single well-defined drug-like structure.
missing_features: Explicit stereoisomers are absent for the branched aryl ketone and aminoalcohol centres, and the recorded formal charges do not establish relevant amine protonation comparisons.
Compact alternatives retaining the favorable aromatic/basic-amine spacing are not consistently preferred over long flexible N-alkyl growth in the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched aryl-ketone/piperidinol compound reaches 0.9999813374312453; the Parent already had nearly saturated scores in other aromatic amine families. Shorter and longer aminoalkyl linkers remain high at 0.997268353359776 and 0.9962324225164898. A conventional piperazine/piperidine member scores 0.9924474921980659. In contrast, a nitro/triazene aromatic compound scores 4.147282724618086e-05 and a urea lacking an accessible aliphatic basic amine scores 9.929936367613832e-05. The observations favor particular aromatic/basic-amine arrangements, but high scores also persist in long-chain dialkylaminoalcohols, including 0.9547669836456144. They do not establish that lipophilic growth improves overall molecular quality.

per_task.generated_character: The best current molecules are aryl sulfonamides attached to piperazine or larger diazacycles, with benzyl benzodioxole, fused aza-aromatic or carbonyl-rich ring partners. A separate high seed-2 family combines an indole-derived fused system, cyclic diones and a methoxyphenol group. Aromatic-token presence is 0.969 and ring-closure presence is 0.9977. These are mainly moderate-sized conventional medicinal frameworks with plausible sulfonylation, alkylation and heterocycle chemistry. Compared with the Parent's aryl pyridone, fused sultam and small sulfonylpiperazine leaders, the current high series retains the same broad aromatic/polar-ring balance while varying attachment topology.
liabilities: Repeated aromatic or sulfonamide addition can increase size and polarity without retaining the favorable attachment pattern.
Nitro-containing, highly charged or hydrazone/guanidine outliers remain in the final proposals, alongside otherwise conventional structures.
missing_features: The best aromatic/polar-ring arrangements have only limited close, simplified alternatives among a much broader stream of less relevant structures.
Defined configurations are absent for the fused saturated indole/dione products; the relatively shallow score differences do not identify a unique missing target fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenylsulfonyl/benzodioxolylmethyl piperazine reaches 0.23462432156460183, compared with the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.20090425134085538. A larger related aryl sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.21309769595029335, so extra aromatic structure is not uniformly helpful. A distinct fused indole/dione family reaches 0.22658333225959595. Long aliphatic amide/ester, carbohydrate-like and small heteroaryl-thiol examples score 0.028602577589751366, 0.034558175818806845 and 0.03934229877866326. These contrasts support a combination of aromatic topology and polar carbonyl/sulfonamide/amine groups rather than any one group alone.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are chemically heterogeneous but mostly recognizable: a diaryl amide/hydroxamic acid, a fluorinated pyrimidinone linked through an aniline to a saturated N/S heterocycle, an aminoalkyl sulfonamide/thiourea, and a benzylated cyclic dione with bromohydrin. Other moderate examples contain amides, aminoalcohols or nitrogen heterocycles. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9494 and ring-closure presence is 0.9759, but the low tail includes very long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like polyamides, elaborate oxygenated polycycles and glycoside/phosphorus hybrids. The Parent also showed diffuse polar aromatic chemistry and severe low-scoring growth. Most leading functional groups are synthetically familiar; growth extremes and unspecified chiral centres are the clearer deficiencies.
liabilities: Unbounded-looking alkyl, peptide-like and heavily functionalized growth produces molecules far outside the size and flexibility of the moderate leaders.
Hydroxamic acid, thiourea, hydrazide and bromohydrin motifs introduce possible chelation, reactivity or stability liabilities, while some late products are highly charged or excessively polar.
missing_features: Consistent compact polar frameworks combining the successful carbonyl, nitrogen and aromatic arrangements are not retained across the broad late proposal stream.
Explicit stereochemical alternatives for the beta-amido centre, hydroxyl-bearing centres and substituted saturated rings are absent; the evidence cannot establish which configuration would matter.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best hydroxamic-acid/amide compound scores 0.26666251850768685, while the fluorinated heterocycle scores 0.26418329062741386 and the sulfonamide/thiourea 0.2614162589649832. The current maxima are below their paired Parent maxima. The digest reports a median of 0.0, and the quoted long-chain, elaborate polycyclic and peptide-like outliers include exact zero scores. Final proposals remain low, from 1.7518667402413673e-13 to 0.0005874138015716985 in the shown excerpt. Moderate-sized polar arrangements are more favorable than these extremes, but the diverse leaders do not establish a necessary fluorination pattern, basic centre or single target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest outliers include very long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like polyamides and large oxygenated or multiaryl assemblies, with exact zero or extremely low scores. Other tasks retain high scores in long-chain dialkylaminoalcohols, so scalar feedback alone does not establish that growth is useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently keep molecular size and repetitive growth near the chemically useful region it has already reached.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide compact analogues, chain shortening and removal of repeated substituents while preserving recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Control chemical complexity independently of occasional high scores assigned to lipophilic growth.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every current digest reports stereocentre-token presence of 0.0, despite high-scoring branched aryl ketones, aminoalcohols, beta-amido hydroxamic acids and fused saturated ring systems. Activated unsaturated nitrile compounds also lack specified alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic molecules without explicitly representing their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow configuration assignment and variation for eligible stereocentres and geometrical isomers, maintaining those identities consistently. The existing trajectories do not establish stereochemical score sensitivity, so any benefit remains an empirical question.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Recognizable aryl carbonyl, fused aza-lactam, sulfonyl cyclic-amine and polar heterocyclic families appear among the leaders, while final proposals can return to unrelated very low-scoring structures. Activated nitrile, hydroxamic acid, thiourea and triazene variants coexist with more conventional alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold diversity is not consistently accompanied by stable close alternatives around favorable local chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate chemically stable matched alternatives that retain useful attachment geometry and donor/acceptor placement, including replacements for reactive unsaturation and labile heteroatom linkages. This would make the favorable regions chemically interpretable without narrowing generation to a named objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fused aza-lactam ester/alkoxy/methylthio variants share 0.6134179161860822, alkyl ketone variants share 0.6118800461361015, and a compact sulfonylpiperazine at 0.23462432156460183 exceeds a larger related member at 0.21309769595029335.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves considerable chemical simplification unexplored where the observed score tolerates peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make smaller substituents, fewer aromatic attachments and stable carbonyl/linker variants readily available around established cores. Near-equivalent score regions can then contain simpler and more plausible compounds rather than mainly additional molecular decoration.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
